title: A counit-normalized chain model for the coinduction tensor comparison
statement:
Let $R\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $U:D(B)\to D(R)$ be restriction on the ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $C_B:D(R)\to D(B)$ be coinduction, right adjoint to $U$, with $C_B(K)$, its action $(b\cdot h)(b')=h(b'b)$, and its evaluation-at-$1$ counit $\epsilon_K:UC_B(K)\to K$ as in [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction]. Put $D_B=C_B(R[0])$, and use the tensor functor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor]. The adjunct of $1_K\otimes\epsilon_{R[0]}$, followed by the unit identification $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R[0]\cong K$, defines a canonical natural transformation
$$\sigma_K:K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D_B\longrightarrow C_B(K).$$
It has the following representative for every $K$. Choose any K-flat complex $F$ [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] representing $K$, any K-injective resolution $R[0]\to J$, and any K-injective resolution $q:F\otimes_R J\to I$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], which exist by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Write $V=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(B[0],J)$, using the product Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex] and the direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Then $I$ represents $K$, $V$ represents $D_B$, and $F\otimes_R V$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(B[0],I)$ represent the source and target of $\sigma_K$ in $D(B)$. The balanced formula
$$t(f\otimes h)(b)=q(f\otimes h(b))$$
defines a $B$-linear chain map between these complexes whose localization is $\sigma_K$. Its counit composite is represented by $f\otimes h\mapsto q(f\otimes h(1))$. After scalar restriction this is the usual Hom/tensor evaluation comparison with these same representatives. The localized comparisons are independent of all the resolution choices, and for every $u:K\to K'$ in $D(R)$ one has
$$C_B(u)\circ\sigma_K=\sigma_{K'}\circ(u\otimes1_{D_B}).$$
No perfectness, flatness or Noetherian hypothesis on $R\to B$, or boundedness of $K$, is assumed; no invertibility of $\sigma_K$ is asserted.

source.place: Tags 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint) and 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext), explicit tensor-counit adjunct on K-flat and K-injective representatives.

proof.text: Write $j:R[0]\to J$ for the chosen resolution. By [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], $1_F\otimes j:F\cong F\otimes_R R[0]\to F\otimes_R J$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Hence $a=q(1_F\otimes j):F\to I$ is a quasi-isomorphism and identifies $I$ with $K$. The resolutions $j,q$ exist by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], specialized to the one-point ringed site. Apply [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] to $J$ and $I$: $V=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(B[0],J)$ represents $D_B$ and $W=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(B[0],I)$ represents $C_B(K)$, with precisely the asserted $B$-actions and evaluation counits. Clause (2) of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor], applied to the $B$-complex $V$ and the K-flat representative $F$, identifies $F\otimes_R V$ with $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D_B$. No flatness of $B$, or K-flatness of $V$ or $J$, enters this application.

source.place: Tags 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint) and 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext); explicit calculation with the stated representatives

proof.text:
For $f\in F^p$ and $h\in V^r=\operatorname{Hom}_R(B,J^r)$ define $t(f\otimes h)(b)=q(f\otimes h(b))$. Additivity and $q(rf\otimes h(b))=q(f\otimes rh(b))$ prove that this descends to the $R$-balanced tensor product; $R$-linearity in $b$ makes the value an element of $W^{p+r}$. The action from [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] gives $t(f\otimes ch)(b)=q(f\otimes h(bc))=(c\,t(f\otimes h))(b)$, so $t$ is $B$-linear. Since $B[0]$ has zero differential, [def-pur-hom-complex] gives $d_Vh=d_Jh$ and $d_W\ell=d_I\ell$. The tensor differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and the chain-map equation for $q$ give
$$d_Iq(f\otimes h(b))=q(d_Ff\otimes h(b))+(-1)^p q(f\otimes d_Jh(b))=t(d_Ff\otimes h+(-1)^pf\otimes d_Vh)(b).$$
Thus $t$ is a chain map. In each total degree the source is a direct sum, so each input has finite support and the displayed prescription requires no exchange of infinite sums and products.

source.place: Tags 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint) and 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext); explicit calculation with the stated representatives

proof.text:
Let $e_J:UV\to J$ and $e_I:UW\to I$ be evaluation at $1$. Direct substitution gives $e_I\,Ut=q(1_F\otimes e_J)$ as chain maps. By [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction], $e_J$ represents $\epsilon_{R[0]}$ with target identified by $j$, and $e_I$ represents $\epsilon_K$ with target identified by $a$. Clause (3) of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] represents tensoring this counit by $1_F\otimes e_J$. In the derived category $[q]=[a][1_F\otimes j]^{-1}$; after identifying $I$ with $K$ via $a$, the counit composite is consequently
$$[1_F\otimes j]^{-1}[1_F\otimes e_J]:K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}UD_B\longrightarrow K,$$
which is exactly the map $m_K=\rho_K(1_K\otimes\epsilon_{R[0]})$ in the statement, with $\rho_K:K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R[0]\cong K$. The adjunction $U\dashv C_B$ in [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] identifies a map $z$ into $C_B(K)$ with $\epsilon_K\,Uz$. Hence $[t]$ is the unique adjunct of $m_K$, namely $\sigma_K$.

source.place: Tags 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint) and 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext); explicit calculation with the stated representatives

proof.text:
Upon restriction to $R$, [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] identifies $UV$ and $UW$ with $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(B[0],R[0])$ and $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(B[0],K)$. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] these use the same K-injective representatives $J$ and $I$. The underlying chain map is
$$F\otimes_R\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(B[0],J)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(B[0],I),\quad f\otimes h\longmapsto(b\longmapsto q(f\otimes h(b))).$$
This is the ordinary Hom/tensor evaluation comparison on those representatives: evaluate $h$ at $b$, tensor with $f$, and apply $q$. The formula is the formula already verified in step 2, so scalar restriction introduces neither another map nor another sign. Step 3 identifies its localization with the canonical adjunct, rather than asserting any invertibility.

source.place: Tags 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint) and 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext); explicit calculation with the stated representatives

proof.text:
The functor and canonical representative comparisons in [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] and [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] identify the source and target objects for any other resolution choices. Step 3 identifies each resulting map with the adjunct of the same $m_K$; injectivity of the adjunction bijection therefore proves independence of all choices. For $u:K\to K'$ in $D(R)$, functoriality of tensor and its unit identification gives $u\,m_K=m_{K'}\,U(u\otimes1_{D_B})$. Naturality of the counit gives
$$\epsilon_{K'}\,U(C_B(u)\sigma_K)=u\,\epsilon_K\,U\sigma_K=u\,m_K,$$
whereas $\epsilon_{K'}\,U(\sigma_{K'}(u\otimes1_{D_B}))=m_{K'}\,U(u\otimes1_{D_B})$. These are equal by the preceding equation. Injectivity of the same adjunction bijection proves $C_B(u)\sigma_K=\sigma_{K'}(u\otimes1_{D_B})$ for every derived morphism $u$, with no need to represent $u$ by a chain map.
